Reaching stability despite adverse events, which arises when a particular environmental challenge meets a particular genetic background.
The removal of unused synapses during development, so that the connections that are used are kept and strengthened.
The startle reflex of the newborn: the arms spread and extend when the infant is startled or the head drops back; normally gone by about 4 months.
A newborn reflex in which the lips pucker in response to a touch around the mouth.
Birth 2 weeks or more after the expected date; the baby often has long nails, little lanugo, more scalp hair and is unusually alert.
Piaget's first period (birth to 2 years), when infants learn through their senses and actions and develop object permanence.
Piaget's period of about 2 to 7 years, with symbols, language and pretend play but not yet logical operations; thinking is egocentric.
Piaget's period of about 7 to 11 years, when children reason logically about concrete things and grasp conservation.
Piaget's last period, from about 11 years, with abstract and hypothetical reasoning about all possibilities.
Knowing that an object still exists when it is out of sight; develops during Piaget's sensorimotor period.
In Piaget's sense, the young child's difficulty seeing a situation from another person's point of view.
How well a child's temperament matches the parents' expectations and caregiving style; a poor fit raises the risk of problems.
One of Thomas and Chess's temperament types (about 15 percent): low activity, withdraws from new things and adapts slowly but does adapt.
Ainsworth's term for the attachment figure from whom a child ventures out to explore and to whom it returns for comfort.
Fear and crying when an unfamiliar person approaches, first seen at about 26 weeks and well formed by about 32 weeks, even in the mother's arms.

Mahler's process, over the first 2 to 5 years, by which the infant emerges from fusion with the mother into a separate self (normal autism, symbiosis, differentiation, practicing, rapprochement, object constancy).
Mahler's subphase at 18 to 24 months, when the toddler swings between independence and closeness, going off and returning to the mother for reassurance.
In Mahler's scheme (2 to 5 years), the child's secure sense that the mother and other key people go on existing and caring when they are absent.
Winnicott's term for a mother who meets the infant's needs well enough, without needing to be perfect.
Winnicott's term for a comfort item, such as a blanket or soft toy, that helps the child bridge the move from the mother to independence.
A pretend friend, common in children of about 3 to 10 years and usually harmless.
The 1 to 5 staging of breast, genital and pubic hair development in puberty (Tanner stages); see Table 32-12.
Bullying carried out through phones, the Internet or social media.
DSM-5 disorder after insufficient care in which a child is overly familiar with unfamiliar adults; it was the disinhibited subtype of reactive attachment disorder in DSM-IV.
